newsitem.title: UK: LME metals follow copper lower by kerb close.
newsitem.headline: LME metals follow copper lower by kerb close.

text.p: Copper dipped to its lowest level for a week on Wednesday afternoon on the LME, but held above the strategic $1,900 level as speculators rushed to offer support, traders said.
The three month market slipped to $1,907 in the afternoon, the weakest level since prices dipped to $1,895 on October 8.
Speculative buying, much of it from North America, propped up the market as it fell towards the psychological $1,900 barrier, one floor trader said.
"I think it was the same specs who were trying to push it through $1,970 yesterday," he said.
Selling pressure re-emerged during the kerb and prices ended $32 weaker at $1,913, but still inside the $1,900-$1,970 range.
Chartists note that the 10-day moving average recently crossed above the 30-day average, which could encourage the bulls despite the loss.
Adding to the bulls' argument are stocks that are expected to continue to decline in the near-term and physical premiums that have ticked higher as scrap supplies remain tight.
But others expect the $1,900 barrier to come under attack soon.
Aluminium also ended off its low, lifting above its nadir of $1,335 in afternoon trading.
Earlier speculative selling was met by solid support at the lows and the market finished at $1,342, down $14.
Many of the others ended weaker, but like aluminium and copper, bounced off their lowest prices.
Lead closed at $741, a loss of $9, but off its low of $737.
Nickel was nearly $100 down at one point, but ended with a $55 loss at $7,065.
Chartists noted the market broke out of its symmetrical triangle formation on the downside, a potentially bearish signal.
Tin finished the late kerb weaker testing support at $5,950. The last trade was at $5,960, down $40.
Zinc was unperturbed by the gyrations of the others, holding to a narrow range and ending $1 up at $1,023.
Alloy ended the day at $1,225/28, down slightly from Tuesday's $1,230.
